notes:
Context: mid-market SaaS vendor that powers in-app search and recommendations for SMB customers. Core product = catalog + Q&A over product docs. Evaluating Redwood Hosted API as fast path, but wants Dedicated for predictable nightly batch runs and sub-50ms similarity queries.

Recent exec notes / call snippets:
- CTO (R. Patel): "We need worst-case similarity lookup < 50ms and average < 20ms for single-shard queries. If Hosted can't meet p99 SLA, Dedicated is compelling."
- Head of ML (A. Gomez): wants end-to-end throughput: 200 QPS for embedding lookups during peak + nightly batch of ~2M items. Concerned about vector DB adapter and TTL for stale vectors.
- Product lead: "We want one billing and one control plane if possible — don't want fragmented tooling across teams."

Technical requirements / evaluation notes:
- Primary integration: Pinecone PoC now; plan to test Milvus on Dedicated if moving forward.
- Batch pipeline: daily pipeline (2M rows) with incremental updates. Looking for advice on batching windows, shard sizing, cold-cache startup cost.
- Throughput target: 150-250 QPS for similarity queries; throughput budget for embeddings generation: ~100k embeddings/day during onboarding ramp.
- Latency SLO: p50 < 10ms (similarity), p99 < 50ms. Acceptable token gen latency for text completion: up to 150ms median for short queries.
- Security: Okta SSO, SOC2 compliance required, audit logs for all token-level requests, KMS for key management, US data residency.
open_questions: Can Hosted API provide stable p99 under concurrent batch window (nightly) without throttling?
